title.narrative: Restoring Dignity and Enabling Resilience: WASH, Shelter and ERL Humanitarian Support for IDPs, Returnees, and Host Communities in Ar-Raqqa, Deir-ez-Zor, Al Hassakeh and Aleppo

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project delivers a principled, protection-centered, multi-sectoral humanitarian response in high-severity, underserved areas of Northern Syria, targeting IDPs, vulnerable host communities, and returnees. In line with 2025 Joint Standard Allocation priorities—ltbgtEnvelope 1lt/bgt (lifesaving multi-sectoral assistance to displaced populations and host communities, 15%) and ltbgtEnvelope 2lt/bgt (support to safe, dignified returns, 85%)—the project provides WASH, Shelter, and ERL support to meet acute needs while fostering resilience and self-reliance.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtIt ltbgtdirectly targets 44,288 individualslt/bgt across priority sub-districts identified in OCHA’s First Standard Allocation Annex 2b, selected based on severity (level 4), displacement/return trends, and service gaps. Implementation will focus on areas with unmet humanitarian needs and CARE presence: ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtltbgtAl Thawrah, Ar-Raqqalt/bgt (PIN: 70,633 38,900 IDPs 1,019 in sites) lt/ligtltligtltbgtDeir-ez-Zor, Deir-ez-Zorlt/bgt (PIN: 253,326 3,293 returnees 805 IDPs, 9,904 in sites) lt/ligtltligtltbgtThiban, Deir-ez-Zorlt/bgt (PIN: 40,924 1,395 returnees 0 IDPs 110 in sites) lt/ligtltligtltbgtMarkada, Al Hassakehlt/bgt (PIN: 40,503 44 returnees 0 IDPs) lt/ligtltligtltbgtMenbij, Aleppolt/bgt (PIN: 257,265 362 returnees 23,967 IDPs 16,793 in sites CARE assessments suggest up to 30,000 returnees) lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtThe response addresses intersecting vulnerabilities. Gender, age, disability, and diversity considerations are fully mainstreamed across the project cycle—from assessments to ME—ensuring inclusive access, participation, and accountability to affected populations (AAP).lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtltbgtKey components include:lt/bgt ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtltbgtWASH:lt/bgt Rehabilitation of water systems in Deir-ez-Zor, Thiban and Markada, where 30,000+ host community members and returnees face critical access gaps due to damaged infrastructure and reliance on costly water trucking. In Al Thawrah, CARE will distribute gender- and age-appropriate hygiene kits to IDPs at Tabqa Sports Center and conduct culturally and environmentally appropriate hygiene promotion to reduce disease risk. lt/ligtltligtltbgtShelter: lt/bgtIn Menbij, support will target vulnerable returnees and host community members, prioritizing female-headed households, large families (+5 children), older persons, and persons with disabilities to enhance safety and housing conditions. lt/ligtltligtltbgtEarly Recovery Livelihoods (ERL):lt/bgt In Menbij, rehabilitation of public market infrastructure will be paired with cash-for-work and vocational training for returnees, youth, women, and PWDs to promote income generation and economic recovery. lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtWASH is prioritized in Ar Raqqa, Deir-ez-Zor, and Al Hassakeh due to widespread infrastructure damage and heightened disease risk. In contrast, Menbij, in Aleppo,offers a stable environment for integrated Shelter and ERL programming to support returns and sustainable recovery. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtInclusive feedback and community engagement mechanisms will be in place, using adapted tools for persons with hearing or visual impairments and confidential channels for women and girls to raise concerns. GBV and child protection risk mitigation will be embedded throughout, with referral linkages to existing services. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtCash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) lt/bgtwill support Shelter and ERL components, empowering household decision-making and stimulating local markets. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtGrounded in the One Syria approach, this project contributes to the SCHF/SHF vision by ensuring a coordinated, integrated response. Activities were designed in consultation with sub-national sectors to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication. ltbrgtBy addressing both urgent and medium-term needs, the project aims to save lives, restore dignity, and support sustainable recovery and resilience in Northern Syria. lt/pgt
